title: VNet: address space, subnets and delegation

videos.script: Every network lesson in this course stands on one thing: a range of addresses. {{range}} In Azure that range is a virtual network. It lives in one region, and it reaches every zone of that region. {{zones}} You choose the range yourself, and one choice is expensive to get wrong. {{overlap}} Two networks that will ever be joined must not share an address. If they do, one of them gets renumbered, with everything in it. {{plan}} Then you cut the range into subnets, one for each kind of thing that needs its own rules. {{subnets}} Azure keeps five addresses of every subnet for itself. A small program of yours will count them. {{five}} Some services want a whole subnet, and a name chosen for them. Some want the subnet handed over to them. That is delegation. {{delegation}} Last, you write the network in Bicep. The compiler checks its shape, and you will see exactly what it does not check. {{end}}
